summary: All three round-3 findings are genuinely closed, each verified by running the exact mutation the round-3 verdict named and confirming a KILL by a SOLE test. 24 mutations run this round; 5 survivors, of which 2 are true equivalent mutants and 3 are reported below as minors. No production defect found: 1,158/1,158 legal values round-trip to identity under the new strict decoder, and every one of 26,112 exhaustive single-byte corruptions plus 400,000 random multi-byte corruptions either raises IOException or yields a fully canonical lease -- there is no input that is accepted lossily. 19 of the 22 tests are demonstrated SOLE killers. Suite 454, 0 failures, 0 skipped; check-tdd green with 22 red records all bound to sha256 c732f434 = the current LeaseTest.java. Tree restored after every mutation; git diff empty and the staged hash unchanged at ae2c8a2e.

findings.title: The UPPER bound of the surrogate range is unpinned. `cp <= 0xDFFF` -> `cp < 0xDFFF` survives all 22 tests and re-opens the round-2 MAJOR verbatim.
findings.failure_scenario:
MEASURED. Mutation: `cp >= 0xD800 && cp <= 0xDFFF` -> `cp >= 0xD800 && cp < 0xDFFF` at Lease.java:110. Result: ./gradlew :format:test --tests binjava.format.LeaseTest -> 22 tests, BUILD SUCCESSFUL. The mutant SURVIVES.

CONSEQUENCE, executed against the mutated class rather than argued:
  new Lease(1, "pod\uDFFFx", "e", 5L)
  CONSTRUCTED: Lease[epoch=1, holderPodId=pod?x, ...]
  ENCODED:     {"epoch":1,"holderPodId":"pod?x","holderEndpoint":"e","expiresAtMillis":5}
  DECODED:     Lease[epoch=1, holderPodId=pod?x, ...]
  IDENTITY?    false
That is word for word the round-2 MAJOR both reviewers found independently -- an unpaired surrogate is not a quote, not a backslash and not below 0x20, getBytes(UTF_8) silently substitutes '?', the round trip is not identity and NOTHING throws -- surviving at the top of the very range the fix installed. It fabricates the holderPodId, the field that answers who may write the commit chain.

WHY IT SURVIVES: the test pins 0xD800 (podId) and 0xDC00 (endpoint). 0xD800 is the lower bound, so `cp >= 0xD800` -> `cp > 0xD800` IS killed (measured). 0xDC00 is interior. Nothing touches 0xDFFF.

NOT A PRODUCTION DEFECT: the shipped code refuses 0xDFFF correctly. This is a test gap at one boundary.

REMEDY (one line, no production change, no new prose): add
  assertThatThrownBy(() -> new Lease(1, "pod1", "e\uDFFF", 5L))
          .isInstanceOf(IllegalArgumentException.class).hasMessageContaining("holderEndpoint");
beside the existing two.

findings.title: Neither end of the control-character boundary is pinned. Both `c < 0x1F` and `c <= 0x20` survive all 22 tests; the first admits a byte that makes the object unreadable to jq.
findings.failure_scenario:
MEASURED, two mutations of Lease.java:86, each run on its own:
  (a) `c < 0x20` -> `c < 0x1F`   -> 22 tests, BUILD SUCCESSFUL. SURVIVES.
  (b) `c < 0x20` -> `c <= 0x20`  -> 22 tests, BUILD SUCCESSFUL. SURVIVES.

(a) is the direction that admits corruption. With it applied, a holderPodId containing U+001F is accepted and written raw into the JSON string literal. RFC 8259 forbids unescaped U+0000-U+001F, and I fed the resulting object to a conforming parser:
  {"epoch":1,"holderPodId":"pod<0x1F>1","holderEndpoint":"e","expiresAtMillis":5}
  -> REFUSED: Invalid control character at: line 1 column 30 (char 29)
So the object round-trips through Lease but jq and every conforming parser refuse it -- which destroys exactly the `cat`-legibility that is the entire stated justification for hand-rolling this codec, and is the same class as the round-1 quote MAJOR. (b) is the over-strict direction: a space in an endpoint becomes illegal, and no test notices.

WHY IT SURVIVES: the hostile array is {pod\"1, pod\\1, pod\u0001, pod\nx}. 0x01 and 0x0A are interior to the range; 0x1F and 0x20 are the two edges and neither appears.

NOT A PRODUCTION DEFECT: `c < 0x20` as shipped is correct. Deleting the guard entirely IS killed, and the quote and backslash clauses are each killed individually (measured).

REMEDY: add "pod\u001Fx" to the existing hostile array -- one array element -- which kills (a). Pinning (b) needs a positive assertion that an endpoint containing a space round-trips, and is the weaker half.

findings.title: The code point the surrogate test uses is misidentified in all three places. `\uD837\uDC00` is U+1DC00, not U+1D800. The test still kills the mutation; the prose asserting which character it uses is false.
findings.failure_scenario:
COMPUTED and cross-checked: Character.toCodePoint(0xD837, 0xDC00) = ((0xD837-0xD800) << 10) + 0 + 0x10000 = 0x1DC00. U+1D800 is the pair \uD836\uDC00. The staged test at LeaseTest.java:287 constructs \uD837\uDC00.

Three places assert otherwise:
  LeaseTest.java:281  "U+1D800 SPECIFICALLY, and it is what makes this test discriminate"
  LeaseTest.java:285  "U+1D800's low 16 bits ARE 0xD800"
  Lease.java:106      "32,768 of 1,048,576 astral code points, 3.13% -- U+1D800 among them, which the test uses"
  backlog.md M4.3     "The test now also uses U+1D800, whose low bits ARE 0xD800"

The BEHAVIOURAL claim is true and I verified it: U+1DC00's low 16 bits are 0xDC00, also inside 0xD800-0xDFFF, so the cast implementation misclassifies it just the same and the mutation `anyMatch(cp -> Character.isSurrogate((char) cp))` is KILLED by this test alone (measured: 22 tests, 1 failed, anUnpairedSurrogateIsRefusedThoughAValidAstralPairIsNot). The 3.13% figure is also right: I counted 32,768 of 1,048,576 = 3.125%.

Only the identity of the character is wrong. Provenance worth naming: the round-3 verdict's own remedy text said 'U+1D800 is \"\\uD837\\uDC00\"', so the reviewer introduced the error and the author copied it faithfully into three files -- the same fix-one-copy-miss-the-duplicates failure mode the M4.0 row records.

This does not weaken any test. It is filed because the packet asks whether the backlog row is honest, and this is the one remaining clause in it that measurement contradicts. REMEDY: either change the literal to \uD836\uDC00 (which I measured also kills the mutation) or change the three comments and the row to say U+1DC00.

verified_closed: ROUND-3 MAJOR (aLeaseTruncatedInsideAStringValue... never reached stringField). CLOSED. Mutation: delete the three lines `if (end < 0) { throw new IOException("lease has an unterminated " + name + ": " + s); }` from stringField. Result: 22 tests, 1 failed, and the sole failure is aLeaseTruncatedInsideAStringValueFailsAsIoNotAnUncheckedException. The new literal {"epoch":1,"holderPodId":"pod1} ends in '}', clears the shape guard, reaches stringField, and StringIndexOutOfBoundsException (unchecked) escapes a method declared throws IOException -- caught. Independently measured, not taken on the author's word.

ROUND-3 MINOR (emoji did not discriminate the cast). CLOSED. Mutation: `cp >= 0xD800 && cp <= 0xDFFF` -> `Character.isSurrogate((char) cp)`. Result: 22 tests, 1 failed, sole failure anUnpairedSurrogateIsRefusedThoughAValidAstralPairIsNot. Confirmed (char)0x1F600 == 0xF600 (Private Use), so the emoji alone would still not discriminate; the added astral value does. See minor F3 for the character's name.

ROUND-3 MINOR R3-F3 (canonical check compared a re-encoding of an already-lossy string). CLOSED. Mutation: revert the strict CharsetDecoder to `new String(bytes, StandardCharsets.UTF_8).strip()`. Result: 22 tests, 1 failed, sole failure aLeaseWithAMalformedUtf8ByteIsRefusedRatherThanSilentlyReplaced.

THE STRICT DECODER BROKE NOTHING THAT SHOULD BE ACCEPTED. Probe over 1,158 legal values -- every 977th code point from U+0020 to U+10FFFF skipping the surrogate block, plus U+FFFD, U+FEFF, U+3000, NBSP, U+2007, TAB, CJK, accented Latin, four astral characters, empty endpoint, leading/trailing/interior spaces, and a 4,096-char value -- constructed, encoded and decoded: 1,158/1,158 round-trip to IDENTITY, zero refused, zero lossy. Blank handling tracks String.isBlank exactly (U+00A0 and U+2007 are not blank and are accepted; SP, U+3000 and TAB are blank and refused).

NO INPUT IS ACCEPTED LOSSILY. Exhaustive single-byte corruption of a canonical lease -- every one of 102 positions x 256 byte values = 26,112 inputs: 24,176 refused with IOException, 1,936 accepted. Plus 400,000 random 1-4 byte corruptions with random truncation: 4,198 accepted. EVERY accepted input is a fully canonical lease that re-encodes byte-identically to what it was given; none carries a replacement character or a lossy field. The accepted-but-different cases are single flips that land on a digit or a name character and produce a different, well-formed lease -- unavoidable in a format with no checksum, and the object store's own integrity check is the right layer for that, not this record. Not a finding.

SOLE-KILLER MAP, 19 of 22 demonstrated by measurement: theEncodingIsExactlyThisByteSequence... (encode field order swapped); aBlankHolderPodIdIsRefused (isBlank->isEmpty); aNegativeExpiryIsRefused (expiry guard deleted); expiryIsDecidedBySuppliedInstant (>= -> >); renewingKeepsTheEpoch... (renew bumps epoch); takingOverBumps... (+1 -> +2); aMalformedOrTruncatedLeaseIsRefused (len<2 -> len<0); anEmptyHolderEndpointIsAccepted... (stringField closing-quote off-by-one); aHolderFieldContainingJsonHostile... (backslash clause dropped); aLeaseTruncatedByASingleByteIsRefused (EACH brace guard deleted individually -- round-2's equivalent-mutant finding is genuinely closed by the message assertions); aLeaseMissingAStringFieldIsRefused (stringField at<0 guard); aStructurallyValidLeaseWithAnIllegalValue... (IllegalArgumentException dropped from the catch); duplicateUnknownOrReordered... (canonical check disabled); anUnpairedSurrogate... (isSurrogate cast, and >0xD800); aLeaseTruncatedInsideAStringValue... (end<0 guard); decodingNullFails... (null check disabled); surroundingWhitespaceIsTolerated... (strip() removed); aLeaseWithAMalformedUtf8Byte... (lenient decoder); aNegativeEpochIsRefused (epoch<0 -> epoch<-1, jointly with aStructurallyValid, and solely under any message mutation since it is the only one asserting the message).

QUESTION 2, THE TWO NON-SOLE KILLERS: I AGREE with round 3's decision not to file them. aLeaseRoundTripsThroughItsEncoding and theEncodingIsReadableJsonAnOperatorCanInterpret are each strictly subsumed -- the first by anEmptyHolderEndpointIsAccepted... and surroundingWhitespaceIsTolerated..., the second by theEncodingIsExactlyThisByteSequence... They still constrain (both fail under many mutations); they are simply never unique. testing.md has no uniqueness rule, and deleting either would remove the plain statement of the record's central property. I found a THIRD in the same category, theFieldInjectionThatWouldFabricateAnExpiredLeaseIsImpossible: its assertion is strictly weaker than aHolderFieldContainingJsonHostileCharactersIsRefused's (type only, no message) and its input's only illegal character is a quote, so it can never be a sole killer. Same judgement -- not filed, it documents the round-1 attack.

QUESTION 4, BACKLOG HONESTY: the two false clauses round 3 named are both corrected. The row now states plainly that the mid-string test was itself an equivalent mutant, that its input was corrected to end in '}' and verified to die (I confirm: KILLED, sole killer), that the 'every astral character' claim was wrong and the true figure is 3.13% (I confirm: 32,768/1,048,576 = 3.125%), that the emoji assertion did not discriminate the cast (I confirm), and it closes with 'Three rounds, and every one found a real defect the previous round's fix had introduced or left'. That is the honest sentence. One clause remains false and is filed as minor F3 -- the character is U+1DC00, not U+1D800.

TIER AND HYGIENE: T0 throughout, correct per testing.md rule 1 -- no socket, no clock, no store. isExpiredAt takes the instant as a parameter (non-negotiable 7) and expiryIsDecidedByTheSuppliedInstantNeverBySystemTime pins it, including the inclusive boundary at exactly expiresAtMillis. No Thread.sleep, no fixed port, no system temp, no mock. No pre-existing assertion weakened: both Java files are new (A), and the only other staged files are two markdown documents, so the check-test-integrity inversion cannot arise.

GATES, RUN NOT ASSUMED: ./gradlew test --rerun-tasks -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL; JUnit XML totals 454 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped (format 144, ingest 84, binstore-backends 86, plugin 34, http 36, binstore-spi 29, sequencer 26, client 15). ./scripts/check-tdd.sh -> ok, 22 new tests, all observed failing first, unchanged since; all 22 red records in .harness/tdd/red.json carry sha256 c732f4341f4d18ff767612208f2da153b178f595678f5667ad3ceebc9c5ad11f, which is sha256sum of the staged LeaseTest.java. Tree restored after each of the 24 mutations; final `git diff` empty and `git diff --cached | sha256sum` = ae2c8a2ea7ef80a9952dff18b43b84c612fcaccc088bfc4a2e86293f0e0eca64, unchanged.
equivalent_mutants_not_findings: Deleting longField's missing-field guard ENTIRELY (not just its message) survives all 22 tests, but it is behaviourally equivalent and cannot be otherwise: with at=-1 the scan starts at a fixed offset, finds no digit, and the `end == from` guard raises the same IOException; and no input lacking the marker can ever be accepted, because the canonical comparison requires the accepted bytes to equal parsed.encode(), which always contains that field. Only the message differs. Contrast stringField's identical-looking guard, whose deletion IS killed -- because there the substring lands on real text and fabricates a holder. No test should be added.
Deleting longField's `end == from` guard survives, as round 3 recorded: Long.parseLong("") throws NumberFormatException, converted to the same IOException by the catch below.
Dropping NullPointerException from decode's catch clause survives: stringField and longField never return null, so the NPE arm is unreachable. Harmless defensive breadth, not a gap.
